summary: Today's news mixes deadly disasters and conflicts worldwide with fresh AI safety and industry controversies, notable science findings, big game release news and Hollywood award highlights.

items.title: Five killed as Russia launches fresh aerial attacks across Ukraine
items.description: Russia's fresh aerial attacks killed five and hit civilian infrastructure across Ukraine, deepening the war's toll.

items.title: Thousands displaced by deadly Indonesia earthquake as rescue efforts continue
items.description: A deadly Indonesian earthquake has displaced thousands and killed at least 51 people as rescues continue.

items.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
items.description: A woman says her stepfather used Grok to turn a childhood photo into explicit imagery, spotlighting AI's abuse risks.

items.title: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
items.description: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed eleven, escalating tensions with Hezbollah.

items.title: Hurricane Lala lashes Hawaii with strong winds and torrential rain
items.description: Hurricane Lala threatens Hawaii with its first direct hit in 34 years, bringing strong winds and torrential rain.

items.title: Twelve killed as Polish bus veers off Hungarian motorway
items.description: Twelve people died when a Polish tourist bus veered off a Hungarian motorway.

items.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work
items.description: Anthropic details how Claude's new text watermarking works, including its resilience to editing and effect on code.

items.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
items.description: SpaceX has officially completed its acquisition of AI coding startup Cursor, folding it into Musk's empire.

items.title: The first anti-AI protester to be jailed has a message for OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta: ‘Regain your humanity’
items.description: The first person jailed for anti-AI protest urges OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta to 'regain your humanity'.

items.title: US to tell partners they must pick sides in AI race with China
items.description: The US is reportedly pressing allies to pick sides in its AI competition with China.

items.title: OpenAI talent exodus raises 'huge red flag' ahead of IPO
items.description: OpenAI's wave of departing talent is raising concerns as the company heads toward a possible IPO.

items.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
items.description: Meta's Zuckerberg claims AI should be 'for everyone,' even as its most powerful model stays locked away.

items.title: Anthropic Risk August 2026 [pdf]
items.description: Anthropic released a new risk report outlining its assessment of AI dangers as of August 2026.

items.title: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, does the West have any influence?
items.description: Five years after the Taliban's takeover, analysts question what leverage the West still holds in Afghanistan.

items.title: From Europe to Asia, floods to heatwaves, world experiences weather shocks
items.description: Floods, heatwaves and wildfires are hitting Europe and Asia simultaneously as extreme weather intensifies globally.

items.title: So much solar: Digging into the list of every US power plant that went online this year
items.description: Data on 2026's new US power plants shows solar and batteries dominating over fossil fuel additions.

items.title: At-home test for infected ticks could improve Lyme Disease diagnosis
items.description: A new at-home test for infected ticks could improve early detection of Lyme disease.

items.title: Abdominal fat predicts heart disease risk better than BMI
items.description: Research finds abdominal fat is a better predictor of heart disease risk than BMI.

items.title: Targeted marine cloud brightening weakens subsequent El Niño
items.description: A study finds targeted marine cloud brightening can weaken the following El Niño event.

items.title: 388 years ago, Galileo worked out why human giants can't exist
items.description: 388 years after Galileo, his reasoning on why giant humans can't exist still holds up physically.

items.description: A former Square Enix executive says killing PlayStation discs could actually lower PS Store prices.

items.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved studio outlines five key updates that'll drop with next week's big patch
items.description: Halo: Campaign Evolved's developer outlines five fixes coming in next week's major patch.

items.description: 2K has launched a new AAA sports studio, Small Axe, based in Vancouver.

items.title: Niko Partners: India games market exceeds $1bn, forecast to reach $1.2bn by end of 2026
items.description: India's games market has topped $1 billion for the first time, growing nearly 15% year over year.

items.description: Compulsion Games appears to have completed its split from Xbox after becoming publisher of South of Midnight.

items.title: ‘The Pitt,’ ‘Hacks’ and ‘Beef’ Among Astra TV Awards Winners

items.title: ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027
items.description: Disney announced a new Monsters, Inc.-themed land opening at Disney World in 2027.

items.description: Lanterns' creators discuss how their grounded take reinvents the Green Lantern mythology for DC's new universe.
